edges.rationale: Named directly by the corpus's own reviewed edge:louis-pasteur-founded-microbiology note as a live, unclosed gap ('co-credited for early microscopy, is still not a corpus node'). Proposed at founded_or_formalized rather than influenced because my recollection of the two source articles is that both apply founder-grade language to him specifically ('father of microbiology'), the same evidentiary shape already accepted for Pasteur and Koch at this exact target -- not because I am defaulting to match their grain without independent consideration. I explicitly considered and rejected two alternative framings before settling here: (a) a narrower concept-level target -- no concept node for 'microscopy' or 'microorganism discovery' exists in this corpus, so there is no narrower grain to route to without inventing a new node the order did not ask for; (b) downgrading straight to `influenced` on the theory that 'discovering microorganisms' and 'founding a discipline' are different acts -- I did not take this path because my recollection of the specific 'father of microbiology' language in both sources is fairly confident, but I flag it heavily below because it is unverified.
edges.uncertainty: This is the most load-bearing generation call in the batch and I am not fully confident in it. What would REFUTE this edge at founded_or_formalized: a live fetch of Wikipedia 'Antonie van Leeuwenhoek' that does NOT contain founder-of-microbiology language, and instead only credits him as an improver of the microscope and first observer of microorganisms without discipline-founding framing -- historians of science do draw a real distinction between him (descriptive, pre-theoretical, two centuries before germ theory, no institutional discipline established) and Pasteur/Koch (who built microbiology's experimental and causal framework), and some sources reserve 'founder' language for the latter pair specifically. If the live text supports only the weaker framing, this should be downgraded to `influenced` rather than admitted at founded_or_formalized, mirroring the corpus's treatment of Fracastoro (influenced, not founded) versus Pasteur/Koch on germ theory. If neither source states any founder-or-influence-grade claim at all, decline outright rather than force it -- the same discipline the corpus already applied to Charles Lyell on uniformitarianism (declined entirely, not merely downgraded) and to von Plenciz on germ theory (declined). Confidence (0.72) is set below the reviewed Pasteur (0.93) and Koch (0.95) edges specifically to encode this unverified-this-session gap, not a belief that the underlying claim is intrinsically weaker than theirs.

notes: Second edge for Leeuwenhoek: considered and DECLINED. I did not propose this edge: the corpus's own reviewed edge:theodor-schwann-founded-cell-biology note already names the specific pre-theory figures it considers relevant to that lineage -- Robert Hooke (coiner of 'cell', 'neither nodified') -- and does not mention Leeuwenhoek at all. I do not have a specific, confident recollection of a source that states Leeuwenhoek influenced or contributed to cell theory as such (as opposed to microbiology/microscopy specifically); proposing that edge anyway would be inventing a connection to fill the 'second edge' slot rather than reporting one the sourcing genuinely supports. Per the order's own standard ('Decline is a first-class outcome'), I am declining rather than manufacturing a second edge.
